# Artifact Keeper 1.7.7

A patch release on the 1.7 line with **one data-loss fix you should read before upgrading**, one security fix, and a reporting fix. No schema migrations.

## Read this first — Maven storage GC could delete hand-repaired objects

If you have ever repaired a Maven 404 by inserting a row into `maven_flat_object_owner`, **that object may already be gone**.

Since 1.7.0 the orphan Maven flat-object sweep enumerated its delete candidates from `maven_flat_object_owner` and tested only catalog anchors. But an owner row is also what makes a legacy row-less object *readable*, and inserting one is the documented remediation for keys the catalog-only backfill cannot see. For exactly that class every arm of the predicate was true by construction and permanently, so **the row that made an object servable was the row that queued it for deletion**. An operator who fixed a fail-closed 404 by attributing the key got a 200 for one hour, then lost the bytes.

**Two changes close it:**

1. The sweep now reclaims only rows the system wrote and can re-derive — `primary_row`, `metadata_files`, `derived_checksum`, `metadata_rollup`, `write_claim`. An operator-inserted row is a primary record, and **any source value the system does not write is now protected**.
2. The sweep is **opt-in**, behind `MAVEN_FLAT_GC_ENABLED`. Unset, it reports what it would reclaim and deletes nothing — matching the OCI blob sweep's posture of biasing toward leaking storage over losing data.

**Affected versions:** 1.7.0 through 1.8.0. Before 1.7.3 the candidate scan frequently never completed on large attribution tables, largely masking it; the 1.7.3 guard rebuild made the scan complete, so **an operator who upgraded to 1.7.3+ for those guard fixes received mass reclamation of hand-repaired data as a side effect.**

**If you may be affected:** there is no recovery from within Artifact Keeper — the sweep hard-deletes the object and its attribution row together, with no tombstone or journal. Recovery depends on storage-side retention: object versioning, a lifecycle noncurrent window, a bucket replica, or a filesystem backup. Each reclaim emitted `Storage GC: reclaimed orphaned row-less Maven flat object` at INFO with the `storage_key`, so a backend log with sufficient retention reconstructs the key list to restore from.

The same fix ships on the current line as **1.8.1**.

## Security

**RUSTSEC-2026-0258** — the bundled `h2` HTTP/2 implementation is updated from 0.4.13 to 0.4.16, closing an unbounded-empty-DATA-frame denial of service. Worth taking promptly on any instance whose gRPC port is reachable from an untrusted network: `tonic` serves h2c only, so the frame decoder is reached **before any application authentication runs**. Upstream rates it Low — the frames are empty, so an attacker trades bandwidth for per-frame bookkeeping rather than payload.

## Fixed

**Proxied downloads are counted again** for Docker/OCI, cargo, NuGet, Debian, Helm and Go, joining the formats that already recorded them. A class-level guard now fails the build if a new proxy serve path records nothing without an explicit marker.

Note that surfacing those counts in the artifact listing arrived in 1.8.0 and is **not** on this line, so 1.7.7 records the data without displaying it in that view. Upgrading to 1.8.1 shows the counts, with the history recorded from this release onward intact.
